text: Joule heating is used everywhere. Heaters, irons and kettles use nichrome, an alloy with high resistivity and a high melting point. A fuse does the opposite job: a short tin lead wire that melts and breaks the circuit when the heating gets dangerous. And the Nepal Electricity Authority bills you in kilowatt hours: one kilowatt hour is three point six million joules.
